title: How do you build a training matrix for a school?
description: Build a school training matrix: child abuse reporting, child safe standards, screening checks, Title IX roles, student records and teacher training by market.
shortAnswer: A school training matrix is built by separating screening gates, such as Working with Children Checks, from training duties, then listing every role with contact with children against the child protection, student privacy, sex discrimination and teacher development rules of each jurisdiction where the school operates. Each cell records the hours or interval the rule sets, the trigger that restarts it, and the record a regulator or inspector can ask to see.
keyTakeaways: School duties attach to contact with children, not job title, so caretakers, coaches, contractors and volunteers can carry the same reporting duties as teachers.
Screening and training are different columns: a Working with Children Check is a clearance to verify and record, while child safe and mandated reporter rules require actual training.
A few school rules fix the clock, such as Pennsylvania's three hours every five years and Illinois's three month and three year cycle; Title IX and FERPA set none.
Title IX training is a specialist duty for coordinators, investigators, decision-makers and informal resolution facilitators, and the materials must be kept seven years and posted online.
As at November 2026, the Title IX recodification, the transfer of Victoria's Child Safe Standards to the Social Services Regulator and Queensland penalty changes all affect school rows.

sections.heading: Why can't a school reuse a generic staff training plan?

blocks.text: Because most school duties are triggered by contact with children and are set by state, province or prefecture rather than by a national employment rule. A generic plan built around job titles misses the bus driver, the sports coach and the contracted tutor, all of whom may sit inside a child protection rule.

The base method in [how to build a training matrix](/guides/how-to-build-a-training-matrix) still holds: people on one axis, obligations on the other, a frequency and an evidence rule in each cell. A school adds two things. First, a screening layer that gates entry before any training starts. Second, a contact flag on every person, so a child protection duty follows whoever works with students. Schools that also run early learning rooms should read the [childcare training matrix](/guides/how-to-build-a-training-matrix-for-a-childcare-service), and those with a tertiary arm the [university matrix](/guides/how-to-build-a-training-matrix-for-a-university).

sections.heading: Which training obligations apply to schools in each market?

blocks.text: Build the columns from the regulation pages for each jurisdiction where the school has a campus. The summaries below use only facts recorded on those pages; follow each link for the full requirement.

items: **United States, Pennsylvania.** Section 1205.6 of the Public School Code requires school entities and their independent contractors to give employees with direct contact with children at least three hours of child abuse recognition and reporting training every five years, with online delivery permitted. School entity includes public, charter, cyber charter, private and nonpublic schools, intermediate units and area career and technical schools. Willful failure to report is a misdemeanor of the second degree, rising to a felony of the third degree in defined cases ([US school mandated reporter training](/regulations/us-school-employee-mandated-reporter-training)).

**United States, Illinois.** Under the Abused and Neglected Child Reporting Act, as reproduced by the Department of Children and Family Services (DCFS), mandated reporters train within three months of engagement and at least every three years after. School personnel, including administrators and certified and non-certified employees, are mandated reporters, and each signs an acknowledgment statement before employment ([US school mandated reporter training](/regulations/us-school-employee-mandated-reporter-training)).

**United States, federal.** 34 CFR 106.45(b)(1)(iii) requires training for Title IX Coordinators, investigators, decision-makers and informal resolution facilitators on the definition of sexual harassment, the scope of the program, the grievance process and impartiality. In K-12, notice to any employee of an elementary or secondary school counts as actual knowledge, and a hearing is optional but written relevant questions are required ([Title IX](/regulations/title-ix-training-requirements)). FERPA sets no explicit training duty, but 34 CFR 99.31(a)(1)(ii) requires reasonable methods so school officials see only records in which they have a legitimate educational interest ([FERPA](/regulations/ferpa-staff-training)).

**Australia, Victoria.** Child Safe Standard 8 requires organizations to equip staff and volunteers to keep children safe through ongoing education and training; its compliance indicators include a training register and policy training on induction and at regular intervals. The Standards are law for organizations required to comply ([Victoria Child Safe Standards](/regulations/victoria-child-safe-standards-training)). Registered nurses are mandatory reporters under section 182 of the Children, Youth and Families Act 2005 ([mandatory reporting](/regulations/mandatory-reporting-training-australia)).

**Australia, screening in three states.** NSW employers verify each worker's clearance online and record the result; Victorian organizations may engage only a person with a clearance, a pending application or an exemption; Queensland organizations link each worker to their blue card account and keep an employee register ([Working with Children Checks](/regulations/working-with-children-check-requirements)).

**Japan.** Teacher license renewal was abolished from July 1, 2022. Article 22-5 of the Act on Special Provisions concerning Education Public Servants requires the appointing board of education to keep a training record for each public school principal and teacher for training taken from April 1, 2023. Induction (Article 23), mid-career (Article 24) and remedial training (Article 25) remain statutory ([Japan teacher training](/regulations/japan-school-teacher-training-requirements)).

sections.heading: Which school intervals come from the rule and which must the school set?

blocks.text: Only a handful of school rules state a number, so tag each cell with whether its clock is statutory or chosen. Where the school chooses, write the reasoning in the matrix, because an inspector will ask why the interval is what it is.

items: **Statutory clocks.** Pennsylvania sets a minimum of three hours every five years. Illinois sets initial training within three months and refreshers at least every three years. Japanese induction training runs for one year from appointment, and remedial training may not exceed one year, extendable to two.

**Event triggers.** Victoria's guide expects induction before work with children begins and again when roles change. A new Title IX appointment is a natural trigger for role training, and the school can require it before the person acts on a case.

**No clock at all.** Title IX names training content but no interval, and FERPA has no training duty. Victoria's indicators say training should be offered regularly and reviewed and updated, without setting a period. These are the cells where a documented school choice is required; see [how to set mandatory training refresh cycles](/guides/how-to-set-mandatory-training-refresh-cycles).

**Screening clocks.** NSW clearances are verified again after each five year renewal, and Victorian workers must notify the regulator within 21 days of starting child-related work. These belong in the screening columns, not the training columns.

sections.heading: Where do Working with Children Checks fit in the matrix?

blocks.text: Treat them as entry gates that must be green before any child-related row can start, not as training. The library's screening page is explicit that a Working with Children Check is a clearance, so the matrix should track verification dates and expiry, not course completion.

items: **NSW.** Employers record the worker's full name, date of birth, check number, verification date and outcome, expiry date and paid or volunteer status, and cannot self-verify. Only workers shown as Cleared or Application in progress may be engaged.

**Victoria.** Organizations check that the worker has added the organization's name and should record number, expiry date and card type. Teachers registered with the Victorian Institute of Teaching are exempt from holding a check unless given an exclusion, so the matrix should record which exemption applies.

**Queensland.** Failing to have a worker hold a blue card and be linked before starting carries 200 penalty units, and failing to keep the employee register carries 50 penalty units, with a penalty unit of $172.70 from 1 July 2026.

sections.heading: What records will inspectors and regulators expect from a school?

blocks.text: Expect requests for what was taught and to whom, not only who finished a course. Several school rules regulate the content or format of the record itself.

items: **Title IX.** 34 CFR 106.45(b)(10)(i)(D) requires all materials used to train the four specialist roles to be kept for seven years and published on the school's website, or made available for inspection where there is no website.
**Illinois.** The mandated reporter acknowledgment statement is signed before employment and retained permanently by the employer, and reporters report training completion to the employer.
**Victoria.** Compliance indicators for Standard 8 include a training action plan, a training register and supervision that identifies training needs.

**Japan.** The MEXT guideline says the statutory training record should be retained for a considerable period, ideally from entry to the present, and that training volume is not directly reflected in personnel evaluation.

**FERPA.** 34 CFR 99.32 requires a record of each request and disclosure, kept with the student's records as long as they are maintained. The [audit preparation guide](/guides/how-to-prepare-training-records-for-an-audit) shows how to assemble these records.

sections.heading: Which school rule changes should be in the matrix now?

blocks.text: Several school rows changed during 2026, so update them with an effective date rather than overwriting the old rule. As at November 2026, the regulation pages record these changes:

items: **February 2026, Victoria:** responsibility for the Child Safe Standards, the Reportable Conduct Scheme and the Working with Children Check transferred to the Social Services Regulator.
**9 March 2026, Japan:** MEXT revised its teacher indicator guideline, which boards use when setting training plans.
**1 July 2026, Queensland:** the penalty unit rose to $172.70, lifting the blue card penalties for organizations.
**July 2026, Victoria:** Working with Children Check reforms allow child safety risk information to be considered in assessments.

**29 September 2026, United States:** the Recodification of Title IX Rules took effect, restoring the 2020 text. The vacated 2024 requirement to train all employees on hire and annually no longer applies, so remove any row built on it.
**October 2026, Victoria:** version 6 of the guide for creating a Child Safe Organisation was published.

blocks.title: Watch items
blocks.text: Illinois DCFS and the State Board of Education have announced a fully redesigned mandated reporter training, and the NSW Office of the Children's Guardian compliance and enforcement policy is under review in 2026. Track both until their effect on school rows is clear.

sections.heading: How does Knowledge Foundry approach this?

blocks.text: Knowledge Foundry records each school obligation with the roles and contact level it applies to, the learning outcome it requires and the assessment point that evidences it, so a change such as the Title IX recodification flags the affected rows. Screening gates are held separately from training so each can be reported on its own. See [compliance programs](/programs/compliance).

faqs.q: Do volunteers belong in a school training matrix?
faqs.a: Yes. Victoria's Child Safe Standard 8 applies to staff and volunteers, and Victorian clearances distinguish volunteer cards from employee cards. Give volunteers their own row so the matrix can show both the screening gate and the child safety training each one completed.

faqs.q: Does every US school employee need Title IX training?
faqs.a: Under the 2020 rule restored in September 2026, the defined training duty applies to the Title IX Coordinator, investigators, decision-makers and informal resolution facilitators. However, in K-12 notice to any employee counts as actual knowledge, so a school may choose to brief all staff on how to pass on reports and record that choice as school policy.

faqs.q: Can one child protection course meet several jurisdictions?
faqs.a: Only partly. Pennsylvania sets a three hour minimum, Illinois sets its own cycle and topics, and Victoria expects training tied to the school's own Child Safety and Wellbeing Policy. A shared core can work, but the matrix should record which local module satisfies which rule.

faqs.q: How does a Japanese public school teacher's training record differ from a completion log?
faqs.a: The record under Article 22-5 is kept by the appointing board of education, not the school, and is used in guidance conversations based on indicators and training plans. A school matrix should therefore link to the board's record rather than duplicate it.
